stem: A substrate settles and becomes noticeably denser during the crop cycle while the irrigation program remains unchanged. What root-zone effect should be evaluated?
choices: Changes in pore structure, drainage, aeration, and water retention that may make the original irrigation assumptions less accurate
Only the fertilizer label because physical media changes do not affect irrigation
Only canopy color because root-zone structure cannot change after transplant
Whether EC meters should be replaced with light meters
rationale: Settling and compaction can alter pore structure and therefore change drainage, aeration, and water retention. Irrigation assumptions should be rechecked when media physical behavior changes.
